anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level statement or transaction design forces the engine to touch far more data and keep transactions open longer than the business case requires.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer chooses an execution plan that is materially worse than the available alternatives even though statistics are adequate.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Obsolete row versions and rollback information accumulate because background cleaners cannot reclaim them fast enough.

When all three root causes surface together, the database exhibits extreme and erratic response times: the same statement alternates between different and generally poor plans, appears constantly in slow-query logs, and holds locks or snapshots for extended periods. Heap and index sizes grow rapidly, sequential scans become longer, and the optimizer’s cost estimates diverge further from reality, resulting in a vicious circle of plan instability. Autovacuum or equivalent cleaners run almost continuously yet still fall behind, while application sessions experience timeouts, increased dead tuples, and occasional transaction-ID wraparound warnings. Diagnostics simultaneously show bloated tables, exploding version stores, and wide row scans triggered by inefficient application SQL.

Causal chain: overly broad or poorly filtered SQL drives high row churn and large result sets. Because the workload is already heavy, even a minor mis-estimated predicate or missing index causes the optimizer to pick plans that devolve into full scans or nested-loop explosions, inflating execution time and the number of modified rows per statement. Longer-running transactions and higher update/delete volume generate vast numbers of MVCC versions. As cleaners lag, table bloat skews statistics and page density, which feeds back into the optimizer and increases the probability of future bad plans. The growing version store also slows visibility checks, compounding the latency induced by both the workload logic flaw and the sub-optimal plans, ultimately degrading OLTP performance across the system.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time after which a TCP keepalive message that has not been acknowledged by the client should be retransmitted.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP keepalive probe is not acknowledged for tcp_keepalives_interval on systems supporting TCP_KEEPINTVL or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Controls retry timing for keepalive probes used to detect unresponsive client connections.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
